request.question: Compare LoRA, bottleneck adapter tuning, and prefix tuning for adapting a frozen language model; use prompt tuning, IA3, QLoRA, AdaLoRA and DoRA where they clarify the decision. Compare trainable parameterization, training memory, inference integration/latency, and task-quality evidence. Explain limitations and distinguish matched comparisons from results with different models, precision or datasets. Give conditional choices; do not declare a context-free winner.

Compare BM25 sparse lexical retrieval, DPR-style dense bi-encoder retrieval, learned sparse SPLADE retrieval, and ColBERT late interaction for document search. Compare supervision/data needs, lexical versus semantic matching, index/query computational costs, and zero-shot retrieval quality. Discuss domain shift and non-comparable benchmark results; recommend methods conditionally without a context-free winner.

Compare HNSW graph search, IVF-PQ (an inverted file with product-quantized codes), and exhaustive flat vector search for a fixed embedding collection. Use NSG and quantization variants as supporting alternatives. Compare recall/error, memory footprint, build/training costs, and query latency/throughput under stated hardware and metric assumptions. Mark unmatched published results as context and identify limitations; do not declare a context-free winner.

Compare DPO, PPO-style reward-model-based preference optimization, and reference-free SimPO or ORPO for language-model alignment. Compare feedback format, online sampling and model components, training compute/memory and stability, and evaluated preference quality/generalization. Use KTO and IPO to clarify data and objective assumptions. Include limitations and mark incompatible experimental results as context; do not name a context-free winner.

Compare dense Transformer language models, Switch-style sparse expert models, and top-two Mixtral-style mixture-of-experts models. Compare total versus active parameter capacity, training compute and data budgets, routing/communication and serving memory costs, and quality/transfer stability. Use GShard and MegaBlocks to explain systems effects. Include limitations and identify non-comparable model reports; make conditional recommendations without a context-free winner.
